name: Orbital rubbing / eye socket massage
lead: Orbital rubbing, also called eye socket massage, is a bonehacking practice in which a person presses or rubs the area around the eye socket in the belief that doing so can change the shape or position of the orbit and therefore the appearance of the eyes. It is discussed as a non-surgical way to alter eye-area aesthetics.

The bony orbit is a cavity formed by seven distinct bones that protects the eye [1]. No published clinical study that the wiki has located has tested whether manual pressure or massage can remodel the adult orbital bones. Separately, medical literature associates vigorous rubbing of the eye itself with progression of the corneal condition keratoconus [2].

paras: The practice is framed by its proponents as applying manual pressure around the orbital rim or eye socket to alter eye shape. The anatomy involved is a pyramid-shaped cavity opening at the face and tapering toward the back of the skull, whose walls are made of seven bones of different embryological origin [1]. The thin inner wall formed by the ethmoid bone is described as easily fractured in trauma, and the lateral wall as the thickest [1].

No studies found. Medical literature on eye rubbing concerns the cornea rather than the orbital bones: several observational reports and case series cited in the keratoconus literature link frequent or vigorous eye rubbing with onset or progression of the condition, and clinicians commonly advise patients to avoid the habit [2].

Because the practice involves pressure near the eye, ophthalmology sources on eye rubbing are the closest relevant evidence. Reports associate repeated, forceful rubbing with keratoconus, a condition in which the cornea thins and bulges [2]. Orbital anatomy sources also note that conditions affecting orbital contents can lead to loss of vision if untreated [1]. These sources do not address massage around the socket as a technique.

card.summary: Pressing or rubbing the eye socket to reshape the eyes; no studies support bone change, and eye rubbing is linked to corneal problems.
card.note: Eye rubbing is associated with keratoconus in the medical literature.

quick.overview:
Orbital rubbing is a bonehack in which people press or massage the area around the eye socket hoping to change eye shape or the look of the orbit.

No clinical study has tested whether this alters the orbital bones, and community material on it is sparse.
quick.mechanism: Believers' idea is that sustained manual pressure remodels bone around the socket. The orbit is a rigid cavity made of seven bones, and no research has examined remodeling by massage.
quick.risks: Medical sources associate vigorous eye rubbing with keratoconus progression, and the orbit surrounds the eye and optic structures. Pressure near the eye has not been studied as a cosmetic technique.
